agent 1: kids in poverty without families?
agent 2: I already donate time and money. Are these kids from the US?
agent 1: yes, and other places. Only 10 cents a day?
agent 2: I'm not sure, how will it help them?
agent 1: provide basic needs like
agent 2: Who is the organization?
agent 1: save the children...very well know
agent 2: oh, save the children.
agent 1: right. they provide shelter, school, food, clothing...interested in helping?
agent 2: what will my ten cents do?
agent 1: mostly for shelter and food and to a lesser degree education....
agent 2: So how do I donate?
agent 1: easy , contact save the children on the internet
agent 2: So, just get ahold of them?
agent 1: right, give them contact information. do you have a bank account?
agent 2: no, i do not have one
agent 1: Do you have a debit card?
agent 2: nope, only cash
agent 1: thanks for your help
agent 2: have a good night!

Belief.A: I believe I can contribute effectively using my debit card, although I've mentioned I only use cash.
Belief.B: I believe donating to Save the Children could make a difference in kids' lives, although I primarily deal in cash, which complicates things.
Belief.C: I believe that my cash donations might be easily managed online, even though I currently use cash as my primary means of transaction.
Belief.D: I believe the organization might not handle cash donations despite suggesting that online contact can facilitate my contribution.

Desires.A: I want to donate larger amounts than ten cents per day.
Desires.B: I want to find a local organization to support instead.
Desires.C: I want to avoid any further discussion about donations.
Desires.D: I want to understand how my money will positively impact the children.

Intentions.A: I will donate to a different charity that only accepts cash.
Intentions.B: I will borrow a friend’s debit card to make the donation.
Intentions.C: I will consider finding a way to donate cash directly to Save the Children.
Intentions.D: I will not be interested in donating since I don’t have a bank account or debit card.

Emotions.A: I feel very excited about donating with my debit card, even though I didn't mention having one.
Emotions.B: I feel confident in my ability to donate online, even though I don't have a bank account.
Emotions.C: I feel unsure about how to proceed with the donation since I only have cash.
Emotions.D: I feel indifferent because I have so many options to donate easily.

Knowledge.A: I know that the organization is actually focused solely on education rather than food and shelter.
Knowledge.B: I know that only large donations to Save the Children make any real difference for the children.
Knowledge.C: I know that Save the Children is a well-known organization helping children in need, both in the US and internationally.
Knowledge.D: I know that Save the Children uses donations mostly for administrative costs rather than directly helping kids.

Trust.A: I view the persuader as ambiguous in their trustworthiness since they were quick to leave without resolving my concerns.
Trust.B: I view the persuader as not entirely credible because they didn't offer an alternative method to donate without a bank account.
Trust.C: I view the persuader as somewhat trustworthy, but I have doubts since they couldn't address the cash donation issue.
Trust.D: I view the persuader as trustworthy because they seem knowledgeable about the organization and its benefits.
